# Volume 3 — Chapter XXIII Cedric Cannot Find the Rock People

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

During that summer, living in Brierley proved to be exceedingly delightful, even if Nell felt pursued by a feeling that “something gone which should be there,” right in the middle of all her holiday pleasures. She refused to confess, even within her most private thoughts, that Hugh’s absence brought this about. Nevertheless, whenever she was forced to trek back home by herself following prayer meetings and B.V.I.S. pow-wows, while Isolde together with Gideon, alongside numerous other happy pairs, dawdled down the dark, star-filled rural lanes, her heart suffered a strange, solitary pang that she was unable to clarify. Hugh refrained from even sending her letters, though she had anticipated he perhaps would. She was aware that he sent notes to Isolde now and then, yet she refused to ask regarding him; meanwhile Isolde, assuming that Hugh corresponded with Nell, offered no news. Hugh’s mother—a cheerful, open, buoyant woman who lacked an abundance of tact—possessed a most awkward practice of inquiring of Nell, invariably using a distressingly clear tone and invariably in front of a gathering, whether she had received word from Hugh recently. Unfortunate Nell was left to simply flush terribly and mutter, “not very lately,” a response that everyone, Mrs. Carrow as well, interpreted as nothing more than a modest dodge.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0000 }

Aside from that, Nell was fond of her summer. In June, Honora arrived for a joyful stay; then, after her departure, Mr. and Mrs. Stanhope, Cedric and Belinda the Fourth returned “home” covering July and August.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0001 }

Festivities returned to Echo Cottage, and the echoes across the river worked constantly to imitate the laughter sounding within the old garden situated behind the spruces.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0002 }

“Miss Rosalind” was unchanged, other than becoming still more charming and lovely. She was worshipped by Cedric, and the bond they shared was a wonderful thing to observe.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0003 }

“However, I never address her simply as ‘mother,’” he clarified to Nell. “Because, as you understand, teacher, that title is reserved exclusively for my own dear mother, so I am unable to use it for anybody else. Instead, I address her as ‘Mother Rosalind’ and she is second in my affection only to father. In fact—I actually hold her slightly dearer than you, teacher.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0004 }

“And that is precisely how it should be,” Nell replied.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0005 }

At thirteen years of age, Cedric had grown quite tall for his time of life. His face remained as lovely as before, his eyes were just as handsome, and his imagination continued to act like a prism, turning whatever met it into brilliant rainbows. He enjoyed wonderful strolls with Nell through the woods, fields, and along the coast. No two people were ever more completely “kindred spirits.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0006 }

Belinda the Fourth had grown up into a young woman. A massive pompadour was her current hairstyle, and she no longer wore the blue ribbon bows of former times, yet the freckles on her face, the snub on her nose, and the breadth of her mouth and smiles remained completely unchanged.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0007 }

“Miss Harcourt, ma’am, you don’t suppose my speech sounds like a Yankee accent, do you?” she inquired with concern.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0008 }

“Belinda, I fail to perceive it.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0009 }

“I’m truly happy about that. People at home claimed I had one, though I figured they probably merely wished to annoy me. A Yankee accent is something I don't desire. I have nothing at all against the Yankees, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. They are genuinely civilized. However, I would choose old St. Brendan’s Island over them any day.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0010 }

Cedric passed his initial two weeks at Brierley alongside his grandmother Stanhope. Upon his arrival, Nell was present to greet him, discovering that he was filled with intense excitement to reach the beach—where Nora, the Golden Lady, and the Twin Sailors would be located. Waiting to consume his evening meal was almost impossible for him. Was it not possible for him to glimpse Nora’s fairy-like face looking around the headland, gazing for his arrival with longing? Nevertheless, the Cedric who returned from the beach at dusk was extremely subdued.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0011 }

“Was your search for your Rock People unsuccessful?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0012 }

With a sorrowful gesture, Cedric tossed his chestnut curls.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0013 }

“Both The Twin Sailors and the Golden Lady failed to arrive,” he remarked. “Nora was present—however, Nora has altered, teacher. She has become different.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0014 }

“Oh, Cedric, it is you who are changed,” Nell said. “You have become too old for the Rock People. They only care for children as playfellows. I fear that the Twin Sailors will never come to you again in the pearly, enchanted boat featuring the sail of moonshine; and no longer will the Golden Lady play for you on her golden harp. Even Nora will not meet with you much longer. You have to pay the penalty for growing up, Cedric. You have to leave fairyland behind.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0015 }

“The pair of you speak just as much nonsense as you always have,” stated aged Mrs. Stanhope, partly with fondness and partly with admonishment.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0016 }

“Oh, no, we don’t,” Nell said, solemnly shaking her head. “We are becoming extremely, extremely clever, and it is a great shame. We are not nearly as captivating once we discover that speech is provided to allow us to hide what we think.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0017 }

“However, it is not—we are granted the ability to share what we think,” Mrs. Stanhope stated in all earnestness. Having no knowledge of Tallyrand, she failed to comprehend epigrams.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0018 }

Nell passed two weeks of blissful days at Echo Cottage during the peak of a sunny August. During this visit, she managed by chance to quicken Ludovic Speed’s slow courtship of Theodora Dix, an event properly detailed in a different account of her life.(1) Arnold Sherman, an older acquaintance of the Irvings, was staying there during that period as well, contributing significantly to the overall enjoyment of their time.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0019 }

(1 Chronicles of Brierley.)
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0020 }

“This has been such a lovely time to play,” Nell remarked. “My strength feels completely renewed. And just two weeks remain before my return to Portmaris, Wexcombe, and Tabby’s Place. Miss Rosalind, Tabby’s Place is the most beloved location. It feels to me as though I possess a pair of homes—a home at Grey Shutters and another at Tabby’s Place. But where did the summer vanish? It feels as though no time at all has passed since my arrival home on that spring night bearing the Mayflowers. During my childhood, I was unable to perceive the far end of summer. The time lay out ahead of me like a period without end. At present, ‘’tis a handbreadth, ’tis a tale.’”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0021 }

“Nell, do you and Hugh Carrow remain as close friends as you once were?” Miss Rosalind inquired softly.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0022 }

“Miss Rosalind, my friendship with Hugh remains unchanged from what it always was.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0023 }

A shake of her head was Miss Rosalind's reply.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0024 }

“I observe that a problem has arisen, Nell. I will be intrusive and inquire about its nature. Have the two of you had a disagreement?”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0025 }

“No; the issue is simply that Hugh desires a deeper connection than friendship, which is something I am unable to provide.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0026 }

“Nell, are you certain about that?”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0027 }

“Completely certain.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0028 }

“I’m extremely, extremely sorry.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0029 }

“I wonder why everyone appears to believe that I should wed Hugh Carrow,” Nell stated in an irritated manner.
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0030 }

“For the simple reason that you were created and destined for one another, Nell—that is the reason. There is no need for you to throw back that youthful head of yours. It is the truth.”
{: #nw-v03-c23-p0031 }
